final_answer: The Rosetta Stone is a pivotal artifact that enabled the decipherment of Egyptian hieroglyphics. It features the same text in three scripts: Ancient Greek, Demotic, and hieroglyphics. Since Greek was already understood, scholars could compare the scripts to decode hieroglyphs. Jean-François Champollion used this method, recognizing that hieroglyphs combined symbolic and phonetic elements. By matching Greek names (like Ptolemy and Cleopatra) to their hieroglyphic counterparts, he unlocked the phonetic system, transforming hieroglyphs from an undecipherable script into a readable language. This breakthrough revolutionized Egyptology, allowing access to ancient Egyptian texts and culture.
